## Description
A skull too large to be a man's or any wolf's, grey as old iron, with deep empty orbits, but light enough to lift with two fingers (Book V ch. 28). In Book VI ch. 18 it is cracked, with a round hole through one eye socket. It rests on a flat stone or pine stump on a bog-island in the [Dykra](../places/dykra.qmd).

## Power
The brotherhood's oath-stone. A wolf who lays both hands on it swears the nine laws of the Pack's Word, and every sworn wolf from the Neman to the Narew hears a lie spoken there (`power_systems.md` §5; Book VI ch. 5). Its keeper is the Wolf-Father, later once the Wolf-Mother.

## Rule & cost
Rules sworn on it, such as "no Gediminid blood" (Book III ch. 15), bind even the guilty. The keeper is chosen by the Root-Mother in the bog (Book IV ch. 6). A wolf is laid to the bog, never burned, and the skull goes down last.

## Origin
[Saga] Found by Lizdeika where the dream-wolf stood after Gediminas's dream on the Šventaragis hunt, 1323, hard and grey as iron (`iron_wolves.md` §3.2). He carried it into the Dykra and the packs swore on it.

## Arc across the books
- **Vilkatai, 1323-1450.** Graph holder; Lizdeika's hundred.
- **Kuolas, 1345.** The Wolf-Father presides at Šešiapirštis's oath over it (Book VI ch. 5).
- **Pušis, 1405-1415.** It lies on a stump while Žiežirba swears (Book III ch. 9, Dec 1405) and while Pilkoji is chosen and takes it up (Book IV ch. 6, 1415-16).
- **Pilkoji, 1415-1449.** She keeps it in the oldest bog.
- **2 Nov 1449.** On Vėlinės she carries it to the deepest water and lies down with it on her chest. The bog closes over her (Book V ch. 28). With it goes the last office of the brotherhood.
